question: How much did prices rise on average in Malaysia in 2022, and why?
answer: Headline inflation in Malaysia averaged 3.3% in 2022 due to a combination of supply and demand factors [1]. These included high global commodity prices, prolonged supply-related disruptions, a sustained US dollar strength against the ringgit, domestic food supply shortages, and seasonal factors, alongside improved demand conditions following the economy's reopening [1].
cited: BNM Economic and Monetary Review 2022 p.37

question: Berapakah kadar inflasi purata Malaysia pada tahun 2022 dan apakah puncanya?
answer: Kadar inflasi purata Malaysia (inflasi headline) pada tahun 2022 adalah sebanyak 3.3% [1]. Puncanya adalah gabungan faktor bekalan dan permintaan, termasuk harga komoditi global yang tinggi, gangguan bekalan yang berpanjangan, kekuatan nilai US dolar berbanding ringgit, kekurangan bekalan makanan domestik, faktor musiman, serta peningkatan keadaan permintaan susulan pembukaan semula ekonomi Malaysia [1, 3].
cited: BNM Economic and Monetary Review 2022 p.37

question: By how much did Malaysia's economy expand in 2022?
answer: Malaysia's economy expanded by 8.7% in 2022 [2, 4].

question: How fast did the economy grow in 2023 and what held it back?
answer: The Malaysian economy grew at a moderate pace of 3.7% in 2023 [5]. Growth was held back by the external front, where net exports contracted as exports declined amid weaker external demand and the global technology downcycle [5].
cited: BNM Economic and Monetary Review 2023 p.28

question: Mengapakah pertumbuhan ekonomi Malaysia lebih perlahan pada tahun 2023?
answer: Pertumbuhan ekonomi Malaysia menjadi lebih perlahan pada tahun 2023 kepada 3.7% disebabkan oleh penguncupan eksport bersih akibat permintaan luaran yang lebih lemah dan kelembapan kitaran teknologi global [1]. Selain itu, penggunaan swasta menjadi sederhana berikutan luputnya kesan langkah dasar kerajaan pada tahun 2021 dan 2022 [1].
cited: BNM Economic and Monetary Review 2023 p.28

question: What was Malaysia's GDP growth in 2024 and what drove it?
answer: Malaysia's economy grew by 5.1% in 2024, up from 3.6% in 2023 [3]. This growth was driven by improvements in domestic demand, which was underpinned by both private and public sector expenditure, alongside a rebound in net exports [3].
cited: BNM Economic and Monetary Review 2024 p.28

question: Berapakah pertumbuhan ekonomi Malaysia pada tahun 2024?
answer: Ekonomi Malaysia mencatatkan pertumbuhan sebanyak 5.1% pada tahun 2024 [1, 2, 5]. Pertumbuhan ini lebih tinggi berbanding 3.6% pada tahun 2023 [1, 2, 5], didorong oleh permintaan domestik yang lebih kukuh dan pemulihan eksport [1].
cited: BNM Economic and Monetary Review 2024 p.23

question: How fast did the economy grow in 2025?
answer: The Malaysian economy expanded by 5.2% in 2025, compared to 5.1% in 2024 [3]. This growth was anchored by resilient domestic demand, driven by continued household spending and investment activity [3].
cited: BNM Economic and Monetary Review 2025 p.25

question: Ekonomi Malaysia berkembang berapa peratus pada 2025?
answer: Ekonomi Malaysia berkembang sebanyak 5.2% pada tahun 2025 [2].
cited: BNM Economic and Monetary Review 2025 p.25

question: What growth does Bank Negara expect for 2026?
answer: Bank Negara Malaysia projects that the Malaysian economy will grow between 4% and 5% in 2026 [3, 4, 5].

question: Berapakah unjuran pertumbuhan ekonomi Malaysia bagi tahun 2026?
answer: Ekonomi Malaysia diunjurkan berkembang antara 4% dan 5% pada tahun 2026 [2].
cited: BNM Economic and Monetary Review 2025 p.57

question: What inflation rate does BNM expect in 2026?
answer: Core inflation is projected to average between 1.8% and 2.3% in 2026 [1]. Meanwhile, core inflation is also expected to remain stable and close to its long-term average [2].
cited: BNM Economic and Monetary Review 2025 p.59; BNM Monetary Policy Statement, 6 Nov 2025 p.1

question: What was average inflation in 2023?
answer: In 2023, headline inflation averaged at 2.5% [5].
cited: BNM Economic and Monetary Review 2023 p.37

question: What was average inflation in 2024?
answer: Headline inflation averaged 1.8% in 2024, which is below its historical average [3].
cited: BNM Economic and Monetary Review 2024 p.38

question: Berapakah purata inflasi pada tahun 2024?
answer: Headline inflasi pada tahun 2024 mencatatkan purata sebanyak 1.8% [1]. Manakala, inflasi teras (core inflation) juga mencatatkan purata sebanyak 1.8% bagi tahun yang sama [1].
cited: BNM Economic and Monetary Review 2024 p.38

question: Why was inflation so low in 2025?
answer: Headline inflation in 2025 moderated to average at 1.4%, driven by improved global supply conditions and the disinflationary impact of domestic policy adjustments [1]. Lower global commodity prices and easing energy costs reduced fresh food and administered prices, while lower production costs were reflected in a 2% decrease in the Producer Price Index [1]. Additionally, the design of domestic policy reforms—such as electricity tariff restructuring and the BUDI95 fuel subsidy programme—successfully cushioned households from policy impacts [1].
cited: BNM Economic and Monetary Review 2025 p.35

question: When did Bank Negara cut the OPR to 2.75%?
answer: Bank Negara Malaysia reduced the Overnight Policy Rate (OPR) to 2.75% in July 2025 [1, 4].

question: Bilakah BNM menurunkan OPR kepada 2.75%?
answer: Bank Negara Malaysia (BNM) telah menurunkan Kadar Dasar Semalaman (OPR) sebanyak 25 mata asas kepada 2.75% pada bulan Julai 2025 [1, 3].

question: When did BNM start raising interest rates after the pandemic?
answer: BNM started raising the Overnight Policy Rate (OPR) in May 2022, following a gradual and measured approach to monetary policy normalisation as the economy recovered [1, 4].

question: When was the OPR raised to 3%?
answer: The Overnight Policy Rate (OPR) returned to the pre-pandemic level of 3.00% by May 2023 [1].
cited: BNM Economic and Monetary Review 2023 p.57

question: Bilakah OPR dinaikkan kepada 3 peratus?
answer: OPR dinaikkan kepada 3.00 peratus menjelang Mei 2023 [2]. Keputusan ini dibuat pada mesyuarat Jawatankuasa Dasar Monetari (MPC) Bank Negara Malaysia pada 3 Mei 2023 [1].
cited: BNM Monetary Policy Statement, 3 May 2023 p.1; BNM Economic and Monetary Review 2023 p.57

question: How did the 2024 diesel price change affect inflation?
answer: The diesel price subsidy rationalisation in 2024 had a modest and contained direct impact on headline inflation [2, 3]. This was due to effective government mitigation measures—such as continuing subsidised diesel for major commercial users under SKDS 2.0 and exempting non-commercial diesel users in Sabah and Sarawak—which minimized cost impacts on businesses and curbed profiteering [2, 3].

question: Apakah kesan perubahan harga diesel pada 2024 terhadap inflasi?
answer: Perubahan harga diesel pada 2024 (melalui rasionalisasi subsidi diesel bersasar pada Jun 2024) memberi kesan langsung yang sederhana terhadap inflasi tajuk utama kerana langkah mitigasi yang berkesan oleh kerajaan [2, 5]. Ini termasuk penyediaan subsidi berterusan kepada pengguna komersial utama di bawah SKDS 2.0 dan pengecualian untuk pengguna bukan komersial di Sabah dan Sarawak [2]. Tindakan ini mengehadkan limpahan kos kepada perniagaan dan harga CPI yang lebih luas [2].
cited: BNM Economic and Monetary Review 2024 p.38

question: How did the ringgit do against the US dollar in 2024?
answer: In 2024, the ringgit recorded an overall year-on-year appreciation of 2.7% against the US dollar [2]. It was one of the few currencies in Asia to appreciate against the US dollar that year [2].
cited: BNM Economic and Monetary Review 2024 p.22

question: Bagaimanakah prestasi ringgit berbanding dolar AS pada 2025?
answer: Pada tahun 2025, ringgit merekodkan peningkatan sebanyak 10.2% berbanding dolar AS menjelang akhir tahun [4]. Prestasi ini disokong oleh aliran modal masuk, prospek ekonomi domestik yang positif, serta pelonggaran dasar monetari oleh bank pusat utama [4].
cited: BNM Economic and Monetary Review 2025 p.19

question: Why did the 2023 subsidy changes barely move inflation?
answer: The implementation of the 2023 domestic policy and subsidy rationalisation measures had a manageable impact on inflation due to the relatively smaller weight of electricity in the Consumer Price Index (CPI) basket, and because the majority of households remained shielded from tariff adjustments [4]. Additionally, the removal of price controls had a minimal impact on fresh chicken prices, which had already trended below the ceiling price beforehand amid stable supply conditions [4].
cited: BNM Economic and Monetary Review 2023 p.37

question: What was special about business investment in 2024?
answer: In 2024, real gross fixed capital formation (GFCF), or overall investment, surpassed pre-pandemic levels in the first quarter and expanded robustly in the subsequent quarters [3]. Investment growth exceeded its long-term averages and outpaced private consumption [3].
cited: BNM Economic and Monetary Review 2024 p.89

question: What does BNM expect from the RON95 subsidy cut and the SST expansion?
answer: Bank Negara Malaysia anticipates that the RON95 subsidy rationalisation and SST expansion will result in some short-term price increases [1], but their overall effects on underlying inflation are assessed to be limited, temporary, and well-contained [1, 3]. The direct impact of these policy measures is expected to dissipate within a year [3], with headline and core inflation projected to average between 2%–3.5% and 1.5%–2.5% respectively in 2025 [3, 5].
cited: BNM Economic and Monetary Review 2024 p.5; BNM Economic and Monetary Review 2024 p.14

question: Apakah jangkaan BNM tentang kesan pengembangan SST dan rasionalisasi subsidi RON95?
answer: Bank Negara Malaysia menjangkakan kesan pengembangan SST dan rasionalisasi subsidi RON95 terhadap inflasi adalah bersifat sementara, terkawal, dan boleh diuruskan [1, 2, 4]. Kesan langsung langkah-langkah dasar ini dijangka mereda dalam tempoh setahun apabila kesan asas berkurangan [4], manakala kesan tidak langsung kepada harga barangan lain juga sebahagian besar kekal terhad [4].
cited: BNM Economic and Monetary Review 2024 p.47

question: How fast did lending to businesses and households grow in 2024?
answer: In 2024, outstanding business loans grew by 5.1% (compared to 3.7% in 2023) [1], while outstanding household loans grew by 5.9% (compared to 5.6% in 2023) [2].
cited: BNM Economic and Monetary Review 2024 p.41; BNM Economic and Monetary Review 2024 p.40
